introduction: I work at the intersection of academic research and industry, focusing on intelligent localization, multi-sensor fusion, and embedded AI. My research connects algorithm development with embedded system design to bring positioning and sensing capabilities to wearable and IoT platforms.
researchOverview: My broader research interests span sensing and navigation for mobile and autonomous systems, with an emphasis on real-time state estimation, embedded intelligence, and hardware–software co-design.
researchBackground: My research focuses on intelligent localization and embedded sensing, spanning multi-sensor state estimation, real-time pedestrian dead reckoning, and wearable positioning systems. I approach these problems through hardware–software co-design, considering localization accuracy, computational cost, energy consumption, and system integration.

Recent contributions include an embedded inertial positioning module, real-time motion estimation on IoT hardware, and a wearable–cloud architecture for continuous indoor–outdoor localization. My broader research interests include on-device AI and efficient learning-based methods for positioning on resource-constrained platforms.

I received my Ph.D. in Computer Science from KAIST in 2026, following an M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering from KAIST in 2020. Earlier research addressed LoRa-based sensing and control for agriculture and machine learning for Vietnamese Sign Language translation.
